nodes.summary: For real $a > 0$ and $b > 0$, the beta function $B(a, b) = \Gamma(a)\Gamma(b)/\Gamma(a + b)$ satisfies $B(a + 1, b) = B(a, b) \cdot \frac{a}{a + b}$.
nodes.title: Recurrence for the beta function in the first argument

nodes.summary: Let $a, b > 0$ be real, $n, k$ natural numbers, $m = n - k$ if $k \le n$ and $m = 0$ otherwise, and $\theta$ real. Write $f_{a,b}$ for the $\mathrm{Beta}(a, b)$ density (zero outside $(0, 1)$) and $B$ for the beta function. Then the density $f_{a,b}(\theta)$ times the probability that the binomial kernel at $\theta$ gives exactly $k$ successes in $n$ trials equals…
nodes.title: Beta prior times binomial likelihood

nodes.summary: Let $a, b > 0$ be real, $k, m$ natural numbers and $\theta$ real. Write $f_{a,b}$ for the $\mathrm{Beta}(a, b)$ density (zero outside $(0, 1)$) and $B(a, b) = \Gamma(a)\Gamma(b)/\Gamma(a + b)$ for the beta function. Then $f_{a,b}(\theta) \, \theta^k (1 - \theta)^m = \frac{B(a + k, b + m)}{B(a, b)} f_{a + k, b + m}(\theta)$.
nodes.title: Conjugacy of the beta density

nodes.summary: Let $a, b > 0$ be real, $n, k$ natural numbers and $B(x, y) = \Gamma(x)\Gamma(y)/\Gamma(x + y)$ the beta function. Under a $\mathrm{Beta}(a, b)$ prior on the success probability, the marginal probability (the evidence) that the binomial kernel gives exactly $k$ successes in $n$ trials is $\binom{n}{k} \frac{B(a + k, b + n - k)}{B(a, b)}$, where $n - k$ is truncated at $0$.
nodes.title: The beta-binomial distribution

nodes.summary: Let $a, b > 0$ be real. Under a $\mathrm{Beta}(a, b)$ prior on the success probability, the probability that a single trial of the binomial kernel succeeds is the prior mean $a / (a + b)$.
nodes.title: Prior predictive probability of a success

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the binomial kernel sends a real $\theta$ to the binomial distribution $\mathrm{Bin}(n, p)$ on $\mathbb{N}$, the law of the number of successes in $n$ independent coin flips with success probability $p$, where $p$ is $\theta$ clipped to $[0, 1]$.
nodes.title: Binomial likelihood kernel

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with $\alpha_i > 0$ for every $i$. Drawing a parameter $\theta$ from the Dirichlet distribution $\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$ and then one label from the categorical likelihood with parameter $\theta$ gives the label $i \in \{0, \dots, n\}$ with probability $\alpha_i / \sum_j \alpha_j$, which is the mean of $\theta_i$ under $\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$.
nodes.title: Prior predictive of the Dirichlet–categorical model

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the categorical likelihood is the kernel from parameters $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ to labels $\{0, \dots, n\}$ that sends a probability vector $\theta$ (all $\theta_i \ge 0$ and $\sum_i \theta_i = 1$) to the law of one label drawn with probability $\theta_i$ for label $i$, and sends every other $\theta$ to the point mass at label $0$.
nodes.title: The categorical likelihood

nodes.summary: For $n, N \in \mathbb{N}$, the multinomial sampling model is the kernel from parameters $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ to sequences $s = (s_0, \dots, s_{N-1})$ of $N$ labels in $\{0, \dots, n\}$ that sends a probability vector $\theta$ (all $\theta_i \ge 0$ and $\sum_i \theta_i = 1$) to the law of $N$ independent draws from $\theta$, which gives $s$ probability $\prod_{m < N} \theta_{s_m}$, and sends every other…
nodes.title: The multinomial sampling model

nodes.summary: Let $m_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ and $v_0, v > 0$, and write $N(\mu, s)$ for the Gaussian law with mean $\mu$ and variance $s$. Let $\pi = N(m_0, v_0)$ be the prior on the parameter $\theta$, let $K$ be the Gaussian likelihood with noise variance $v$, so that $K(\theta) = N(\theta, v)$, and let $Q$ be the normal posterior kernel, $Q(x) = N(\mu(x), s)$ with $\mu(x) = (v m_0 + v_0 x)/(v_0 + v)$ and $s = v_0 v/(v_0 + v)$. For…
nodes.title: Disintegration of the Normal–Normal joint law

nodes.summary: For a sequence $s = (s_0, \dots, s_{N-1})$ of labels in $\{0, \dots, n\}$ and a label $i$, the count $n_i(s)$ is the number of positions $m < N$ with $s_m = i$.
nodes.title: Label counts

nodes.summary: Let $m_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ and $v_0, v > 0$, and write $N(\mu, s)$ for the Gaussian law with mean $\mu$ and variance $s$. If the parameter $\theta$ has prior $N(m_0, v_0)$ and the observation given $\theta$ has law $N(\theta, v)$ (the Gaussian likelihood with noise variance $v$), then the marginal law of the observation is $N(m_0, v_0 + v)$.
nodes.title: The marginal of the data

nodes.summary: Let $m_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ and $v_0, v > 0$, and write $N(\mu, s)$ for the Gaussian law with mean $\mu$ and variance $s$. Take the prior $N(m_0, v_0)$ on the parameter $\theta$ and the Gaussian likelihood $\theta \mapsto N(\theta, v)$, and let $\mu(x) = (v m_0 + v_0 x)/(v_0 + v)$ and $s = v_0 v/(v_0 + v)$. For Lebesgue-almost every observation $x$, a new observation drawn from the likelihood, with $\theta$…
nodes.title: Normal–Normal posterior predictive

nodes.summary: With noise variance $0$, the Gaussian likelihood sends each $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ to the Gaussian law with mean $\theta$ and variance $0$, which is the point mass at $\theta$: the observation is the parameter.
nodes.title: Noiseless Gaussian likelihood

nodes.summary: For a noise variance $v \ge 0$, the Gaussian likelihood is the kernel from $\mathbb{R}$ to $\mathbb{R}$ that sends a parameter $\theta$ to the law of the observation $x \sim N(\theta, v)$, the Gaussian with mean $\theta$ and variance $v$: for $v > 0$ it is the measure with the $N(\theta, v)$ density with respect to Lebesgue measure, and for $v = 0$ it is the point mass at $\theta$.
nodes.title: Gaussian likelihood with known variance

nodes.summary: Let $m_0, \theta, x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $v_0, v > 0$, and write $\varphi_{\mu, s}(y) = (2 \pi s)^{-1/2} \exp(-(y - \mu)^2 / (2 s))$ for the density of the Gaussian with mean $\mu$ and variance $s$. With $\mu(x) = (v m_0 + v_0 x)/(v_0 + v)$ and $s = v_0 v/(v_0 + v)$,
nodes.title: Completing the square

nodes.summary: For variances $v_0, v > 0$, the posterior variance $s = v_0 v/(v_0 + v)$ satisfies $s^{-1} = v_0^{-1} + v^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Precisions add

nodes.summary: For a variance $v \ge 0$, write $\varphi_{\theta, v}(x) = (2 \pi v)^{-1/2} \exp(-(x - \theta)^2 / (2 v))$ for the density at $x$ of the Gaussian with mean $\theta$ and variance $v$, read as $0$ when $v = 0$, with values in $[0, \infty]$. Then $(\theta, x) \mapsto \varphi_{\theta, v}(x)$ is a measurable map on $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Measurability of the Gaussian density in its mean and argument

nodes.summary: Let $m_0, x \in \mathbb{R}$, $v_0 > 0$ and $v \ge 0$. The posterior mean $(v m_0 + v_0 x)/(v_0 + v)$ equals $m_0 + \frac{v_0}{v_0 + v}(x - m_0)$: it moves from the prior mean $m_0$ toward the observation $x$ by the gain $v_0/(v_0 + v)$.
nodes.title: Posterior mean as a gain update

nodes.summary: For a prior mean $m_0 \in \mathbb{R}$, a prior variance $v_0 \ge 0$, a noise variance $v \ge 0$ and an observation $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the posterior mean is $(v m_0 + v_0 x)/(v_0 + v)$, taken to be $0$ when $v_0 = v = 0$. When $v_0 + v > 0$ it is the precision-weighted average of $m_0$ and $x$.
nodes.title: Posterior mean of the Normal–Normal model

nodes.summary: For variances $v_0, v \ge 0$, the posterior variance is $\frac{v_0 v}{v_0 + v}$, taken to be $0$ when $v_0 = v = 0$. In the normal–normal model with prior variance $v_0$ and known noise variance $v$, this is the variance of the posterior of the mean after one observation.
nodes.title: Posterior variance of the normal–normal model

nodes.summary: Let $m_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ and $v_0, v \ge 0$, let $s = \frac{v_0 v}{v_0 + v}$ be the posterior variance and, for $x \in \mathbb{R}$, let $\mu(x) = \frac{v m_0 + v_0 x}{v_0 + v}$ be the posterior mean (with $0 / 0 = 0$). The kernel from $\mathbb{R}$ to $\mathbb{R}$ sends $x$ to the measure with density $\theta \mapsto \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi s}} e^{-(\theta - \mu(x))^2 / (2 s)}$ with respect to Lebesgue measure. For…
nodes.title: Candidate posterior kernel of the normal–normal model

nodes.summary: Let $a, b > 0$ be real and $k \le n$ natural numbers. For the binomial kernel and a $\mathrm{Beta}(a, b)$ prior, the posterior distribution (Mathlib's posterior kernel) after observing $k$ successes in $n$ trials is $\mathrm{Beta}(a + k, b + n - k)$.
nodes.title: Beta–binomial conjugacy

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with $\alpha_i > 0$ for every $i$, and let $s$ be a sequence of $N$ labels in $\{0, \dots, n\}$ with label counts $n_i(s)$. Under the multinomial sampling model with the Dirichlet prior $\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$, the posterior distribution of the parameter after observing $s$ is the Dirichlet distribution with parameters $\alpha_i + n_i(s)$.
nodes.title: Dirichlet–multinomial conjugacy

nodes.summary: Let $m_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ and $v_0, v > 0$. Take the prior $N(m_0, v_0)$ on the mean $\theta$ and the likelihood under which an observation $x$ has law $N(\theta, v)$. Then for Lebesgue-almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the posterior distribution of $\theta$ given $x$ is the normal law with mean $\frac{v m_0 + v_0 x}{v_0 + v}$ and variance $\frac{v_0 v}{v_0 + v}$.
nodes.title: Normal–Normal conjugacy with known variance

nodes.summary: Let $a, b > 0$ be real and $k \le n$ natural numbers. Under a $\mathrm{Beta}(a, b)$ prior on the success probability, after observing $k$ successes in $n$ trials of the binomial kernel, the posterior predictive probability that one further trial succeeds is $(a + k) / (a + b + n)$.
nodes.title: Posterior predictive of the beta-binomial model

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with $\alpha_i > 0$ for every $i$, and let $s$ be a sequence of $N$ labels in $\{0, \dots, n\}$ with label counts $n_i(s)$. Under the multinomial sampling model with the Dirichlet prior $\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$, drawing a parameter from the posterior after observing $s$ and then one label from the categorical likelihood gives the label $i$ with probability…
nodes.title: Posterior predictive of the Dirichlet–multinomial model

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the probability vectors are the $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with $\theta_i \ge 0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_i \theta_i = 1$; they form the parameter space of the categorical model.
nodes.title: Probability vectors

nodes.summary: For every $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ and every sequence $s$ of $N$ labels in $\{0, \dots, n\}$ with label counts $n_i(s)$, the likelihood $\prod_{m < N} \theta_{s_m}^+$ of $s$ equals $\prod_{i = 0}^{n} (\theta_i^+)^{n_i(s)}$ as extended nonnegative reals, where $x^+ = \max(x, 0)$.
nodes.title: The sequence likelihood depends only on the label counts

nodes.summary: For $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ and a sequence $s = (s_0, \dots, s_{N-1})$ of labels in $\{0, \dots, n\}$, the likelihood of $s$ is the extended nonnegative real $\prod_{m < N} \theta_{s_m}^+$, where $x^+ = \max(x, 0)$.
nodes.title: Likelihood of a label sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with $\alpha_i > 0$ for every $i$, and let $s$ be a sequence of $N$ labels in $\{0, \dots, n\}$ with label counts $n_i(s)$. The Dirichlet distribution $\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$ weighted by the density $\theta \mapsto P_\theta(s)$, the probability of $s$ under the multinomial sampling model with parameter $\theta$, equals $B(\alpha + n(s)) / B(\alpha)$ times…
nodes.title: Evidence-weighted Dirichlet prior

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
